newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in quiet trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said treasury bills worth Z$158 million were maturing on Wednesday and that the central Reserve Bank had come into the market with an offer for Z$200 million worth of the 91-day paper.
But only about Z$100 million, at 17.60 percent, was taken up.
"The market has been short for the past two days so people are a bit cautious," said one dealer.

Meanwhile, discount houses were selling treasury bills in a 17.50 to 17.60 percentage range from around 17.55 percent on Tuesday while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 17.90 and 17.50 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.25 and 17.55 percent.
NCDs redeemable after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought slightly easier at 18.60 percent from 19 but sold at 18.50 from 18.25 percent while call money shed one percentage point to 18 percent.
Figures from the central bank indicated a market shortage of Z$57 million at the close of trade on Tuesday.
